# dsh-loop-engine-allinone
**English** · 简体中文
**dsh-loop-engine-allinone** is an all-in-one agent loop engine switcher for **DeepSeek Harness** (`
dsh`). It enables per-session engine switching across **10 hosted engines** (Claude Code, Codex, Pi,
Kimi Code, Antigravity, ZCode, Qoder CN, Hermes Agent, Grok Build, MiniMax Code) alongside the buil
t-in `in-process` loop.
> `dsh` is the harness CLI. `dsh --profile <name>` boots one of its **profiles**, and the engine pic
ker plus this plugin's settings page appear in whichever profile renders a web UI (the shipped `web`
template is one; the Desktop app uses `desktop`).
Sessions are fully independent: run Codex in one chat while another runs Kimi Code or Antigravity si
multaneously. Handover between two hosted engines happens seamlessly in place; switching to or from
the native `in-process` engine performs an in-browser reload without restarting the backend process.
All without modifying the DeepSeek Harness core codebase.

> **Fork Note**: This project is a fork of `kuun993/dsh-loop-engine`.
> While the upstream plugin in
troduced per-session switching for 4 initial engines, this fork refactors the internals into a **uni
fied data-driven engine registry** and **shared driver infrastructure**, expanding support to **10 d
ngine registry** and **shared driver infrastructure**, expanding support to **10 distinct engines**.

ngine (Kimi) | **3 engines** (Kimi, Grok, MiniMax) on a shared ACP skeleton |

-hoc implementations | Standardized `driver-cli/` & `driver-acp/` runtimes |

#### Qoder CN: the two hard prerequisites
These belong to the CLI, not to the plugin; the handover cannot remove either.

1. **You must be signed in to Qoder CN.** `-p` runs in the CLI's `local`
provider-access mode, which

requires `isAuthenticated()`. The handover starts
each step by copying `~/.qoder-cn/.auth` into its

private config root; when
that directory is missing the turn fails before a child spawns, with
`QOD

ERCLICN_NOT_LOGGED_IN` and the message to run `qoderclicn login`.
2. **The startup entitlement check

must reach Qoder.** Before custom providers
are allowed, the CLI calls `GET https://openapi.qoder.c

om.cn/api/v3/user/status`
and requires `featureSwitches.allow_byok >= 2`. Offline — or behind a netw

ork
that blocks that host — the check returns null, custom providers are refused,
and no request eve

r reaches the DSH endpoint. **The handover is not an offline
mode.** A failed turn says so in the CL

I's own words; it does not silently
fall back to a Qoder model.

> **ZCode has one prerequisite of the same kind:** the desktop app's
> `resources/config/provider/zc

ode-builtin.json` must be discoverable, because
> the CLI requires the built-in and personal provide

r files in the same breath.
> Install ZCode normally (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ZCode`,
> `%ProgramFi

les%\ZCode`, or `%ZCODE_HOME%`), or point
> `env.ZCODE_BUILTIN_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE` at a catalog yo

urself. A standalone
> `zcode` on PATH with no catalog is not enough for a handover.

The settings page repeats this matrix ("Which engines can run a model configured
in dsh"), so the an

swer is reachable without reading this file.
> **Tool cards.** All ten hosted engines stream `tool/c

all` and `tool/result`
> with the engine's own arguments and output. Hermes Agent and ZCode reach th

is
> through their documented JSONL event streams (`hermes chat -q … --format
> stream-json` / `zcod

e -p … --output-format stream-json`), which are the same
> structured surfaces their desktop apps co

nsume — the old `-z` / plain `-p`
> renderings printed only the final answer.
## Architecture & Extending
Adding a new engine is straightforward thanks to the unified registry:
1. **Register Descriptor**: Add the engine ID to `HOSTED_ENGINE_IDS` and define its metadata and cap

abilities in `src/engine-registry.ts`.
2. **Implement Driver**: Create a driver implementing `runSte

p` (leveraging `src/driver-cli/` or `src/driver-acp/`).
3. **Bind Driver**: Register the driver clas

s in `src/engine-drivers.ts`.
4. **UI Localization**: Add display strings in `src/client/locales.ts`
and an optional SVG icon in `src/client/engine-marks.ts`.
Both tables enforce compile-time exhaustiveness checks — incomplete engine registrations fail at bui
ld time rather than runtime. Detailed instructions are in docs/engine-registry.md.
## Version Compatibility
A single release seamlessly supports multiple DeepSeek Harness generations via runtime detection:
| Plugin release | Supported DeepSeek Harness |

` and `0.2.1` share the last segment because the harness kept the same API shape
across them, so one

range covers both. `dsh`'s compatibility check reads these peers
and refuses to load a plugin that

misses one, which is what made `0.7.3` uninstallable
on `0.2.1`.
See docs/compatibility.md for harness upgrade checklists and API surface diffs.
## Technical Notes & Limitations
- **Agent Factory Replacement**: The plugin registers a unified facade over the harness agent factor
y. Any session that cannot be routed to a hosted engine gracefully falls back to the native `in-proc

ess` loop.
- **Engine State Persistence**: Active session engine bindings are stored in `$DSH_HOME/.

loop-engine/engines.json`. If this file is cleared, sessions revert to their preset defaults.
- **Su
bprocess Concurrency**: Multi-session execution shares the respective CLI's local authentication and

configuration directory.
- **Grok Build Shell Execution**: Grok tools rely on the harness client te
rminal bridge (`ctx.shell`).
